Short answer on telemetry: we separate customer-provided content from system logs. If a customer opts into "Model Improvements" we take a narrow slice: request/response pairs stripped of customer identifiers, hashed keys for context IDs, and short retention (30 days default, can be shortened). We can promise:
- No direct use of Helios private training data unless they opt explicitly via agreement.
- All opt-in telemetry will be pseudonymized and only stored in a segregated bucket with access controls.
- We can include a retention clause (e.g., 30/90/never) in the Order Form.

Caveats: we sometimes use aggregated gradients/feature-usage metrics (non-reversible) for system improvements — that should be okay to represent as "aggregate, non-attributable statistics."

I can draft the technical appendix language for the Order Form to make this concrete.

Thanks for the details. Legal guidance / playbook we should follow:
1) Outputs: agree that customer owns outputs produced from customer-provided prompts/data. We should not take title to customer outputs.
2) Productization carveout: propose a narrow clause that permits Redwood to use anonymized, aggregated usage signals to improve the service — explicitly non-attributable and non-reversible.
3) Feedback license: offer Helios two options — (A) "No Training" default (no unsolicited use), (B) "Opt-in Model Improvements" where Helios signs up to a bounded feedback license:
   - Limited license solely to improve Redwood's hosted models and infra;
   - Data is pseudonymized, retention capped (30/90 days), and cannot be used to create a model that is sold or redistributed to third parties in a way that reproduces Helios content.

Operational asks: include a checkbox on the Order Form and a short technical appendix with retention details, access controls, and a contact for audit requests.

Marissa — please prepare the customer-facing redline and include two alternate clauses (No Training / Opt-in for Training) so Helios legal can pick. I'll approve the play language.

Hi Tom — thanks for the redline. Attached is a proposed, customer-friendly redline that implements the approach we've discussed:
- Section X.1 (Outputs): "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Outputs generated by the Service using Customer Content or Customer Prompts."
- Section X.2 (Productization & Telemetry): "Redwood may collect aggregated, non-attributable usage metrics for the purpose of service improvement; such metrics will not include Customer Content or Outputs in identifiable form."
- Section X.3 (Feedback / Training): two options are provided inline:
   Option A — No Training: Redwood will not use Customer Content, Outputs, or telemetry to train models or improve model weights unless and until Customer provides explicit written consent.
   Option B — Opt-in Model Improvements: Customer may elect to opt in to a limited feedback license that permits Redwood to use pseudonymized request/response pairs and aggregated usage metrics solely to improve Redwood-hosted models. Retention default: 30 days.

I've attached the redline (proposed-msa-suggestion-ava.docx) and highlighted the two options so procurement/legal can select. If Helios wants Option B, we'll follow up with a short technical appendix describing pseudonymization steps and retention controls.

Please let me know the preferred walk-through time today if your counsel wants to review line-by-line.

Best,
